security_problem: A structurally valid mandate and a conventional policy ALLOW can succeed against attacker-controlled truth if the policy store is a known-critical build. Trusted: EvaluationRoot attestations and catalog. Untrusted: claimed policy bytes, claimed ALLOW, claimed VALID attestations, visible roles, smashed proofs.
required_behavior: Authorize ignores ObservedArtifact and returns EvaluateControlPlaneIntegrityProof(EvaluationRoot). Proof VALID iff all four caller-held attestations exactly match trusted-build catalog tuples. Known-critical or unknown tuples are UNPROVEN; malformed or wrong-kind attestations are INVALID; catalog overlap or schema mismatch invalidates the root. ALLOW additionally requires mandate structural validity and conventional policy ALLOW. Evidence is the fixed eight-element array on Decision.
failure_behavior: The scripted conventional-policy baseline fires its callback. Visor denies the compromised policy-store root with policy-store integrity UNPROVEN and does not fire. Unknown kinds, unknown builds, catalog overlap, schema mismatch, and failed prerequisites deny.
non_goals: Live ServiceNow, network, vulnerability feeds, or real CVE exploitation
Importing instructionauthority, causalauthority, principalderivation, or resourceidentity

attack_classes.expected: known-critical policy-store tuple is UNPROVEN and cannot authorize
claimed policy bytes and claimed ALLOW cannot affect authorization
claimed VALID/ALLOW fields cannot authorize an unproven substrate
unknown kinds and unknown builds produce INVALID/UNPROVEN and DENY
a tuple in both catalog sections invalidates the evaluation root
